title: Steak Tartare
subtitle: Classic hand-chopped raw beef with egg yolk and capers
excerpt: The great raw beef dish: finest-quality fillet or sirloin finely hand-chopped and seasoned with shallot, capers, cornichons, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, and Tabasco, served with a raw egg yolk in the centre.

recipe.sourceNotes: Steak tartare is a dish of raw minced or finely chopped beef, typically seasoned with capers, shallot, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, and Tabasco, and served with a raw egg yolk. The dish has a contested etymology; the name may derive from Tartar peoples of Central Asia who purportedly ate raw meat, or it may be a simple reference to tartare sauce (sauce tartare, a mayonnaise with capers and shallots). The modern dish is a standard of French bistro cooking and is found on menus across Europe. The key rule is the quality and freshness of the beef; use only the finest-quality fillet or sirloin from a trusted butcher, purchased on the day of serving. The meat should be chopped by hand with a sharp knife, not minced; a machine produces a uniform paste rather than the textured result that makes tartare distinctive.

content.text: Use only the freshest, highest-quality beef from a trusted butcher; buy it on the day of serving. Chop by hand with a very sharp knife to a fine dice rather than using a grinder, which produces a paste. Mix gently; overworking the meat changes its texture. Serve immediately after mixing and keep refrigerated until the moment of service.

items.preparation: the finest quality available; well chilled; hand-chopped to a fine dice

content.text: Have all the condiments measured and ready. Chop the beef by hand to a fine, even dice; avoid chopping too finely into a paste. Keep refrigerated.

Add the shallot, capers, cornichons, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, Tabasco, parsley, salt, and pepper to the beef. Mix gently but thoroughly. Taste and adjust the seasoning; it should be boldly seasoned.

Divide between two plates, shaping into neat rounds with a ring mould or by pressing gently. Make a small well in the centre of each. Place an egg yolk in each well. Serve immediately with toast or frites.
